sentences.text:
(Presently Lodged At Jodhpur Jail)
 ----Petitioner  Versus State Of Rajasthan, Through Pp  ----Respondent For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Mahender Kumar Dudy.

For Respondent(s) : Mr. P.S. Panwar, P.P.
 HON'BLE DR. JUSTICE NUPUR BHATI Order 08/05/2025 1.
Heard learned counsel for the parties as well as perused the material available on record.

2. The instant application for bail has been filed under Section 483 BNSS on behalf of the petitioner,
who is in custody in relation to F.I.R. No.31/2025 dated 22.03.2025, registered at Police Station GRP Abu Road, District Sirohi for the offence under Section 406, 420, 467, 468, 120-B of IPC.
3.

entities.text: Police Station GRP Abu Road, District Sirohi
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner has falsely been implicated in the case while alleging that the petitioner along with the main co-accused Vikas Singh Rajput has made forged demand drafts and the amount that was to be paid to the Station Superintendent, was not made.

He submits that the main co-accused Vikas Singh Rajput asked the petitioner, who was his employee, to open Bank Account, which would be utilized for making a demand draft for paying an amount of Rs.6,60,194/-.
He submits that the petitioner being employee of the main co-accused did not deny for the same and got the account opened in his name and one Demand Draft was made for the tune of Rs.60,194/-.

He [2025:RJ-JD:22113] (2 of 2) [CRLMB-4633/2025] submits that the petitioner was not aware of the intention of the main co-accused that he would create forged Demand Draft in the name of the petitioner & not deposit for the due payment.
He also submits that the petitioner's name is not present in the FIR.

He further submits that the petitioner is not having Kailashchand vs State Of Rajasthan (2025:Rj-Jd:22113) on 8 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35576664/
1 previous criminal antecedent and the petitioner is in custody since 26.03.2025, thus the petitioner deserves to be enlarged on bail.
4.

Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor opposes the bail application, however, is not in a position to refute the submissions that petitioner's name is not present in the FIR and petitioner is not having previous criminal antecedent.

5. Considering the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor, no useful purpose would be served by keeping the present petitioner behind the bars for further period till disposal of the case and also looking to the possibility that the trial may take long time to conclude
, this Court deems it just and proper to enlarge the petitioner on bail.
6. Consequently, the bail application is allowed.

It is ordered that the accused-petitioner namely Kailashchand S/o Late Shri Ramswaroop, in relation to the F.I.R. No. 31/2025 dated 22.03.2025,
registered at Police Station GRP Abu Road, District Sirohi shall be released on bail; provided he furnishes a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- and two surety bonds of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the learned trial court with the stipulation to appear before that court on all dates of hearing and as and when called upon to do so.
(DR. NUPUR BHATI),J 134-pradeep/-
